justification: Adds cohort tagging to the feedback path so a student class can be told apart from professional users, and adds the two user types that had no representation. Touches a served surface (the feedback widget) but changes no number, no report and no stored answer. Standard because a silent failure here means a cohort's feedback is unattributable and the trial produces nothing.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: NOT SELF-REFERENTIAL: the rule is exercised against inputs a stranger can put in a URL, and must SEPARATE them. It fails if 'uts-16658' is rejected, and equally if any of empty, single-character, leading/trailing dash, a space, a quote-and-comment, markup, or a 60-character string is accepted. An untagged visit must return null rather than a placeholder, because 'unknown' would read as a cohort in the data.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed. The FIRST test helper redefined window.location per test and the suite could not run at all - 84 suites failed, 0 tests. The second attempt did it once with configurable:true and still threw 'Cannot redefine property: location', because the jest setup pins it. Rewritten to drive the query string through history.replaceState, which is also how a real navigation sets it: 14 pass. The control case pins both directions, so a stub returning null always and a stub echoing input both fail. A third defect was found by the operator asking what the URL should visibly DO: nothing did. The tag was invisible, which made the whole mechanism unverifiable without database access. Fixed, and the fix then introduced a hydration mismatch by reading window during render - caught before push and moved into useEffect.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The acceptance set is not invented here: it is what a lecturer can paste into an LMS and what a browser will carry through a redirect. The rejection set is the standard shape of injected input for a value written to a varchar column.

pre_impl.existing_data: auth.users holds ONE row (the founder). property_reports holds 1,347 rows with no owner column - 533 of them carry test/demo/calibration in the address and the busiest non-test address was run 26 times, so they are development output, not users. user_feedback holds 8 rows, most recent 2026-01-30. Its user_type column has NO check constraint (verified against pg_constraint - only severity is constrained), so new values store without a migration.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The brief assumed no accounts, no CRM and no sharing existed. Supabase Auth IS wired with a /login page and a callback route, report sharing IS built, and the feedback system is complete - a widget, a hub and three endpoints - and has simply been unused since January. The gap was never tooling; it was that none of it had been pointed at anyone. Building accounts would have been the wrong answer to the right question.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One new 60-line module and two edits. No accounts, no table, no migration, no API change - the feedback route already spreads `context` into context_data, so the cohort lands there untouched. Ownership on reports was deliberately NOT added: 1,347 reports have survived without it, and adding it before anyone asks is the build-before-distribution trap the idea ledger names.

functions.name: getCohort
functions.what: Returns the cohort code for this browser, read from ?cohort= and remembered, or null.
functions.output: a validated lowercase code, or null
functions.if_none: null, never a placeholder. 'unknown' would read as a cohort in the data and quietly merge every untagged visitor into one group.
functions.edge_cases: Returns null during SSR, where there is no URL and no storage. Swallows a localStorage failure (private browsing) rather than throwing inside a render. Trims and lower-cases so a pasted or wrapped link still matches.
functions.failure_mode: At worst a legitimate visit goes untagged and its feedback lands in the general pool - recoverable by asking. It cannot mislabel one cohort as another, because a code either validates or is discarded.

break_it.scenario: A student opens the lecturer's link, then searches a second address and navigates away from the query string.
break_it.what_happens: A URL-only implementation loses the tag on the second page, so only the first submission is attributable and the trial under-counts itself.
break_it.how: The code is written to localStorage on first sight and read back when the query string is absent.

break_it.scenario: Someone edits the URL to ?cohort=<script> or a SQL fragment.
break_it.what_happens: An unvalidated value is written to a varchar column and later rendered in an internal view.
break_it.how: A conservative pattern - lowercase, digits, inner dashes, 3-40 chars. Eight hostile inputs are fixtures asserting null.

break_it.scenario: A student files feedback and the profession dropdown still says 'Certifier'.
break_it.what_happens: A whole cohort's feedback is filed under a profession none of them hold, and the one field that could separate them is wrong on every row.
break_it.how: 'Student' and 'Academic / lecturer' added, and a tagged visitor defaults to student - including after a successful submission, which previously reset to 'certifier' and would have relabelled every second report.
break_it.repro: read the setUserType calls in FeedbackWidget.tsx - both are cohort-aware

break_it.scenario: The feedback endpoint cannot reach the database during the trial.
break_it.what_happens: Students believe they have reported bugs that were never stored - the worst outcome, because the trial looks quiet rather than broken.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated here and stated: the route builds its own pg Pool from DB_HOST/DB_NAME/DB_PASSWORD, which default to localhost. They are present in .env.local; whether they are set in the Vercel production environment is UNVERIFIED from here. The failure is at least visible - the API returns 500 and the widget alerts the student - but this must be tested against production before a cohort is invited.
break_it.repro: submit feedback on the deployed site and confirm the row appears in user_feedback

break_it.scenario: A lecturer opens the class link to check it worked before sending it to 40 students.
break_it.what_happens: Nothing on screen changes. The code is invisible, so the only way to confirm the tag is being applied is to query the database - and a student has no way at all to know their feedback is grouped.
break_it.how: The closed button shows the code as a chip and reads 'Report an issue' rather than 'Feedback'; the open panel repeats it as 'Tagged to <code>' directly above the form. The link now verifies itself.
break_it.repro: open /assessment?cohort=test-1 and look at the bottom-right button

break_it.scenario: The cohort is read during render instead of after mount.
break_it.what_happens: getCohort() touches the URL and localStorage, neither of which exists on the server, so the server emits 'Feedback' and the client emits the class code. React resolves that hydration mismatch by discarding the client markup - the tag can disappear on exactly the page it is meant to prove.
break_it.how: Moved into useEffect with useState initialised to the untagged values, so server and first client render agree and the chip appears on the second paint.
break_it.repro: grep useEffect in FeedbackWidget.tsx - the read is inside it, not in the component body

post_merge.db_reset: No schema change, no migration. user_type has no check constraint, so 'student' and 'academic' store as-is.
post_merge.watch: SELECT context_data->>'cohort', count(*) FROM user_feedback GROUP BY 1 - should show the cohort code once a class starts, and null for everyone else.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open the deployed /assessment?cohort=test-1. The bottom-right button must read 'Report an issue' with a 'test-1' chip, and opening it must show 'Tagged to test-1'. THEN submit and confirm a row lands in user_feedback with cohort test-1 and user_type student - if the DB_* variables are missing in Vercel this fails and every student's report would be lost.
